name: Ambot Tik
subtitle: a sharp coconut-free fish curry that is exactly what its name says, sour and hot

ingredients.note: traditionally shark or catfish; kingfish or monkfish hold up well
the tik half of the name

ingredients.qty: lime-sized ball, soaked in 200ml hot water

prepNotes: Rub the fish with salt and 1/4 tsp turmeric and rest it 15 minutes — a firm fish takes salt slowly.
Soak the tamarind in hot water while you grind the masala, then squeeze and strain.
There is no coconut in this curry. Do not add any to soften it — the sharpness is the dish.

steps.text: Grind the chillies, garlic, ginger, cumin, pepper, turmeric and coriander powder with the vinegar and 3 tbsp water to a fine paste.
Heat the oil and fry the chopped onion over medium heat for 8 minutes, until soft and pale gold.
Add the masala paste and fry 6-7 minutes until it darkens and the oil beads at the edge of the pan.
steps.tip: Frying the vinegar out is what stops the curry tasting raw. Give it the full seven minutes.

steps.text: Pour in the tamarind water and the rest of the water, add the kokum and salt, and bring to a simmer.
Simmer uncovered 10 minutes so the gravy reduces slightly and turns glossy.
Taste and balance: it should be assertively sour and hot. Add a pinch of salt or a splash of vinegar rather than sugar.
steps.tip: Balance it before the fish goes in — you cannot stir it properly afterwards.

steps.text: Slide in the fish, shake the pan to settle the pieces, and simmer 7-8 minutes until opaque through.
Rest 10 minutes off the heat before serving with plain rice.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and the sourness mellows usefully by day two. Reheat gently to a bare simmer; never boil hard or the fish shreds.
